# Worked example, milestone 3: the L2 rung

Generated by `python scripts/worked_example_m3.py`; every number is computed by code and labelled with its provenance. It continues [`worked_example_m2.md`](worked_example_m2.md), which takes the same design from L1 to measured numbers.

Design: `iterative:data_width=15,n_iter=12,angle_guard=1,frac_guard=0,rounding=round` (the exhaustive winner of `low_area_control`).

## 1. Interface contract (cycle model)

`hw_dse.l2.cycle.CycleModel`: an FSM (IDLE → PRE → 12 × ITER → OUT); latency **15 cycles**, `ready` high only in IDLE, so a new angle every **15 cycles**. *exact* (from the schedule).

Checked against its generated RTL on a 40-angle bursty trace (664 clock edges, Icarus Verilog 12.0): ready mismatches 0, valid_out mismatches 0, output-code mismatches 0. *exact*.

## 2. DDS spectrum of its exact outputs

SFDR **79.8 dBc**, SNR **69.5 dB** (*simulated (hw_dse.l2.dds l2-v1: golden-model DDS, 32-bit phase accumulator, coherent 16384-point FFT, tone bin 1297)*).

## 3. In a bursty system (`bursty_offload`)

System: bursty requests: bursts of 8 (0 ns apart) arriving as a Poisson process, 2 requests/us on average; constraint p99 latency ≤ 0.4 µs.

| metric | L1 (bound) | L2 (simulated) |
|---|---|---|
| sys_p50_latency_us | 0.2975 | 0.3758 |
| sys_p99_latency_us | 0.6001 | 1.183 |
| sys_throughput_msps | 1.954 | 1.954 |

Utilisation 14.8%, deepest queue 25 requests (*simulated (hw_dse.l2.system bursty l2-v1, SimPy 4.1.2; CORDIC clock 198.3 MHz = estimated Fmax)*).

Its throughput (13.2 MSPS, *estimate*) is 6.6x the 2 MS/s average, so the MSPS-only view keeps it as the winner. But one request every 15 cycles means the eighth request of a burst waits for seven others: even an isolated burst (the L1 bound) misses 0.4 µs, and with Poisson bursts overlapping the simulated p99 is 2.0x the bound. Exhaustively, no FSM design meets the constraint; the winner becomes `pipelined_m:data_width=15,n_iter=12,angle_guard=1,frac_guard=0,rounding=round,m=6` (745 LUT+FF vs 251 for the MSPS-only winner), p99 0.195 µs (*simulated*).

## 4. Three views, three winners (`multiaxis_control`)

System: control loop: a tick every 1 us issues 32 requests at once (32 requests/us on average); all 32 results within 0.44 µs of the tick (p99 over ticks).

| view | winner | LUT+FF | sys_p99_batch_us |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSPS-only (≥ 32 MSPS) | `pipelined_m:data_width=17,n_iter=14,angle_guard=1,frac_guard=0,rounding=round,m=7` | 953 | bound 0.5704 / simulated 0.5871 |
| L1 bound | `pipelined_m:data_width=17,n_iter=14,angle_guard=1,frac_guard=0,rounding=round,m=5` | 1013 | bound 0.4342 / simulated 0.4465 |
| L2 simulated (the truth) | `pipelined_m:data_width=17,n_iter=14,angle_guard=1,frac_guard=0,rounding=round,m=4` | 1072 | bound 0.3679 / simulated 0.378 |

The MSPS-only winner meets the 32 requests/µs average, but serving a whole batch of 32 within 0.44 µs needs ((32 - 1) + (4 - 1)) cycles / 0.44 µs = 77.3 MHz even with perfect alignment, and its estimated Fmax is 59.6 MHz. The L1 bound (each tick served alone, starting on a clock edge) admits m=5; the simulation adds clock-edge alignment: a tick lands between CORDIC clock edges, so up to one cycle passes before the first accept, which pushes m=5 just past the deadline and makes m=4 the winner. (No synchroniser is modelled; a real clock-domain crossing would add about two cycles.)

The L2 node makes this switch, and it can only do so because it simulates every L1-feasible design, not the L1 front: with m = 3, 4, 5 of this design evaluated, the L1 front is m=5 alone (m=4 has m=5's numerics, so the same accuracy, and more area), and `l2_select` returns m=4 (2 of 3 L1-feasible designs pass the simulation).
